title: S10: per-file debug viewer — server endpoint + page skeleton
description: User decision 2026-07-22: the per-file revision view is a DEDICATED debug viewer page, not a 'Filename' filter on the main webapp — free to expose engine internals (source attribution, conflict notes, seed hashes). This task: a server endpoint serving one file's revision ladder from the merged multi-source reconstruction (viewer_api_* patterns) plus the debug page skeleton with file selection / deep-link.

title: S10: debug viewer — revision-ladder rendering + DOM tests
description: Render the selected file's revision ladder in the dedicated debug viewer (revision list with source attribution, conflict notes, seed hash where present). DOM tests per existing webapp test patterns for selecting a file and rendering its revision list; manual check against plate_cli.py on the real claude-data sources.

title: S11: per-file sweep harness — run all candidates, emit results table
description: Build the harness that runs the S9 per-file reconstruction for a list of candidate files against the claude-data sources and emits a results table (per file: endpoints matched — baseline blob present and final revision vs current ~/Programming/jot content — plus recovered revision count and gaps). Table lands in plans/166-per-file-target.md. Success bar (user-corrected): all or most revisions recovered, to recreate the commit history lost when the plate branch became corrupted; endpoint matches are necessary, not sufficient.

title: S11: run the M-file sweep (68 files) and triage results
description: Run the task-186 harness over all 68 'modified' files from the S8 enumeration. Record the results table in plans/166-per-file-target.md; itemize every failure/gap as a finding, not an omission. Phase gate: S11 must be complete before the S12 'added' phase starts.

title: S12 prep: prove the iterative reconstruct -> commit -> re-seed loop
description: User workflow: 'start reconstruction from point A (a git hash) up until some chunk of revisions (like 5 or 10 steps), then commit those. Re-attempt reconstruction from this new commit hash, and more revision history will be reconstructed and committed. Repeat until the entire history is restored.' Prove this loop end-to-end on one file (plate_cli.py or a fixture): seed via --repo/--base-commit, reconstruct a chunk, commit it (in a scratch clone, never the real ~/Programming/jot), re-seed from the new hash, and show the second iteration recovers history the first did not. Document the recipe in plans/166-per-file-target.md.

title: S12: 'added' files sweep (11 files, rename/move-aware)
description: Run per-file reconstruction for the 11 'A' files. User: these are probably the result of script executions (rename-file/move-file events); each ladder must start at its rename/move (or born-fresh) origin and include all modifications AFTER the move. Where history is only partially recoverable, apply the task-188 iterative commit-and-re-seed workflow. Results recorded as in S11. Phase gate: after S11, before S13.

title: S13: 'removed' files sweep (52 files, paired with S12 moves)
description: Run per-file reconstruction for the 52 'D' files. Each ladder ends in a true deletion or a move-away; classify each file as true-delete or move-source and name its S12 pair (the A file the content moved to) where applicable — the associated delete events from moves fold into this phase. Results recorded as in S11.

title: Layer 1: anchor selection + pre-anchor stubs with byte-op refusal
description: S2. Per file: anchor = first full-content evidence (commit blob, snapshot, Write body, complete Read echo, populated originalFile); earlier byteless mentions become pre-anchor stub nodes that refuse byte-consuming operations (display/placement only). Unit tests: anchor chosen correctly per evidence class; stub byte-op refusal. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Layer 1: on-disk end-state node + presumed-user-edit gap nodes
description: S2. Append the on-disk end state as the final node; between every adjacent pair with unexplained differing content insert a presumed-user-edit gap node (Q8 invariant: never invent an attribution). Unit tests: end-state node present; gap nodes appear only between differing verified states. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Multi-session merged view + corroboration marks
description: S5. Merge per-session SessionTimelines into one derived view per ReconstructionEntity, nodes ordered by Instant; mark nodes where multiple sessions observed the same bytes as corroborating (input for dashed cross-lane lines). Unit test: interleave by Instant; corroboration mark on same-bytes nodes; single-session degenerate case. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: RenameEdge/CopyEdge extraction + lineageOf walk
description: S6. Extract RenameEdge (timestampOfRename) and CopyEdge (timestampOfCopy) with JsonlRef evidence from layer-1..3 evidence (reuse the engine's existing rename channels); lineageOf walks RenameEdges to derive one continuous history; bornCopy's first content = copiedFrom's reconstructed state at timestampOfCopy. No stored lineage groups. Unit test: rename chain end-to-end; copy fork leaves both lineages independent. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Per-file widgets on one shared vertical time axis with session lanes
description: S8. Each file renders as a rounded widget offset to its history's start on the shared vertical axis, per-session lanes inside. DOM test on a two-file two-session fixture: widget offsets ordered by start Instant; lanes per session. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Dashed cross-lane corroboration lines
description: S8. Render dashed cross-lane lines exactly where S5 corroboration marks exist. DOM test: dashed line present exactly at corroborated Instants. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Layer switcher with tooltips; 5+ disabled until unlocked
description: S9. Layer: [1]..[12] control above the timeline; 1-3 selectable and re-render at that layer's detail; buttons for layers 5 and up disabled until the functionality each enables becomes unlocked for this engine mode; every button gets a tooltip naming what that layer adds (1 start/end, 2 commits, 3 snapshots, 5 derived edits, 7 script runs, 8/9 branches, 10 verified replay, 12 decoration). DOM tests per S9. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Condense toggle: single column with classification + truncated message rows
description: S10. Condense button squashes per-session lanes into a single all-nodes column per file and back; condensed rows look like the current webapp timeline: classification + truncated original message (reuse its row rendering). DOM test per S10. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Kept/ignored dimming + branch end-vs-rejoin rendering
description: S11. Reuse the engine's kept/ignored row classification: ignored nodes dimmed; a branch whose content did not carry forward visually ends, one whose content carried forward visually rejoins — a selection rectangle contains exactly what its patch contains. DOM test with a rewind fixture. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Node click fills Details pane (reused view incl. [{ }] JSON button)
description: S13. Clicking a timeline node fills the top-right pane with the existing webapp Details view (reused, not reimplemented), retaining the [{ }] button that shows the node's raw JSON. DOM test per S13. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Script-run node click shows per-file before/after diffs + script body
description: S15. Clicking a script-run node shows the before/after state of each affected file as a diff in the detail pane (same diff mechanism as segment selection) alongside the script body, laid out per the approved task-214 mockup. DOM test with a fixture containing a script-run node. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Ruler arming + cut marks with per-file at-or-before snap
description: S16. 'Create segments for patch extraction' arms the global left ruler; cut marks (triangles) are one global instant snapping PER FILE, AT-OR-BEFORE, to that file's nearest verified state (Q17a/b: never pull future content backward; unverified or mid-residual cut states refused). DOM test: arming enables marks; unverified-node mark refused; a mark between two files' beacons snaps to each file's own at-or-before verified state. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Segment partition P1..Pn spanning every file's lanes
description: S16. The entire ruler length partitions into segments P1..Pn spanning all files' lanes; segments are selectable. DOM test: n marks yield n+1 contiguous segments covering the full ruler. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Engine: segment patch = per-file diff of snapped states, emitted as git-diff
description: S17. patch = diff(endStateOfPreviousSelection, rightmostStateInThisSelection) per file, each state the at-or-before snapped verified state at the segment's cut; first segment's base = anchor; a file born after the cut is absent and first appears as a creation in the segment containing its birth; concatenate into one git-diff. Unit test: each segment's git-diff applies in sequence via git apply to reproduce the final state, including the born-after-cut-1 file case. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Webapp: segment selection shows its patch in the reused Changes view
description: S17. Selecting a segment computes its task-218 patch and shows it in the reused webapp Changes view (Fork-style tree + diff) in the bottom-right pane, visible only while a segment is selected. DOM test per S17. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Timeline bubble for files with no snapshots/beacons: "no snapshots available"
description: User request (2026-07-24): if a file has no file-history snapshots and is not referenced in any git commit, the webapp timeline should still render the file's bubble like the others in the currently selected layer's view, but with the text "no snapshots available" — indicating to the user that no beacons exist for the file.
